rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are

human.problem: The passage ends mid-argument on David's harsh words ('their backs be bent forever'). Paul's next verse (11:11) answers this right away: 'did they stumble so as to fall? Certainly not!' The passage has no story group, so the 'story isn't over' rule doesn't apply, and the baker leaves on the hardening with no sign the teaching continues.
human.question: When a Letters passage has no story group but its argument clearly continues into the next verse, should the last story card get a line saying the teaching isn't done?
